summary: SSO connector role propagation delay causing 403s for newly provisioned console roles in us-west
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-10 07:00 UTC, a subset of users and service principals provisioned by the SCIM sync are intermittently receiving 403 Forbidden when accessing the internal Console in the us-west region. The error appears for newly provisioned roles only and resolves after a delay (~10-30 minutes) or after a manual role rebind.

Impact: Internal console access blocked for engineers and service accounts that were part of the March role-remap rollout. Affects approx 8-12 users and 3 service accounts in us-west; prevents access to logs and runbooks during the window. No customer-facing impact.

Environment: prod | us-west. Identity stack: Okta SSO -> SCIM provisioner -> identity-service -> console. Recent changes: role-remap policy (#PR6012) deployed 2026-03-09 and SCIM batch window adjusted to smaller batches.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create or rename a user in Okta that triggers the new role mapping (group  internal-ops -> console-admin).
2) Wait for SCIM sync to run (configured batch window).
3) Attempt to log into Console (https://console.us-west.redwood.internal) via SSO.

Expected behavior: Newly provisioned users receive correct RBAC claims on first login and can access Console immediately.

Actual behavior: SSO completes successfully (Okta assertion accepted), but Console returns 403. Identity-service logs show roles not yet present in local RBAC cache for the subject. Access becomes available after cache refresh or manual role rebind.

Observed logs/traces:
- identity-service: WARN role-cache: miss for subject=okta|u12345 trace=trc-0a1b2c3d
- scim-provisioner: INFO batch 472 completed; user u12345 role=console-admin assigned; scim-sync-id=sync-20260310-07
- console: 403 requestId=req-4f6c7d status=403 reason=missing-rbac-claims

Temporary workaround: For impacted users, run the admin command in the identity-console to force a role rebind: POST /admin/force-rebind?user=okta|u12345 or trigger a manual SCIM sync job for the affected batch. We have documented the steps in the runbook.

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: race condition between SCIM provisioner writing role assignments to main store and the identity-service cache invalidation window.
- Reproduced locally by forcing SCIM to fast-path writes: observed identity-service cache miss even though DB contains role record.
- Cache TTL was recently increased from 1m -> 10m to reduce load during peak; this change coincided with the role-remap rollout.
- The batch size reduction in SCIM sync causes more frequent writes; combined with longer cache TTL, this exposes propagation delay.
- No evidence of Okta assertion or SAML issues.

Next steps / proposed mitigation:
1) Roll back cache TTL change for identity-service to 1 minute in us-west and monitor 1 hour.
2) Add a targeted cache-invalidate hook in the SCIM provisioner after role assignment writes (short-term patch).
3) Add additional metrics/tracing for role write->cache visibility latency.
4) Update runbook with manual rebind steps and who-to-page.

Owner: identity-team (assignee above).

Resolution notes: Pending. Patch for cache-invalidate is in progress (PR referenced above). Will update when rollback or patch is in prod.
